acceptance.text: Hard proof: four recto-only pages hold 9 unique panels in 17 occurrences in the flattened Z order A B C D E F G H X H G F E D C B A (p1 ABCD, p2 EFGH, p3 X HGFE, p4 DCBA); X is the single hinge, occurs once, and is the first panel of page 3 directly after the page 2 to 3 turn; A opens and closes the book. Verified from layout.json, the page PNGs and the film's edit list, not from the plan.

Section 7 fixture on real exports: validate.py passes [A,B,C,X,C,B,A] as single-centre and rejects [A,B,C,X,C,B',A] when B' changes one balloon word or one drawing pixel; on the actual page PNG every mirrored pair (i,16-i) has byte-identical panel crops, and in the actual mp4 every mirrored pair plays the identical canonical frame sequence (panel layer, before camera) and identical sound cue; the run is recorded in symmetry.json against the registry revision after every export.

Blind reading: a reader who is not told the symmetry key, reading the page at normal pace (and separately watching the film once), points to X as the turning panel and says that the repeated first/last panel (the porter's outstretched arm, 'YOU! STAY RIGHT THERE.') means something different: an accusation at the start, protection from whoever is behind the door at the end. The back half is not described as a rewind or a mere repeat.

Genuine material and animation: every visible element is handmade (polygon silhouette puppets with visible scissor-jog edges, pins and punched lace; bell, door, bench, key, envelope; hand lettering) or foraged with a recorded free licence in films/credits/cercle-vicieux.json (LoC profile heads printed solid black, archive or Commons sound); no filter or reference tracing. In the film, panels A and X at least are animated frame by frame on twos: limbs rotate about their pins without detaching (pin error <=1 px), the bell swings and decays with clapper lag, and in X the hand-shadow pulls the cord twice and the bell answers each pull. A viewer sees things move with weight, not pans and fades over stills.

Once means once: the hand behind the frosted glass is clearly readable as a hand gripping a cord (thumb distinct, not a blob) in X and appears in no other panel; the service door is never drawn open; the frosted pane in A, G and E is plain lit glass. A viewer can say 'someone is behind the glass' at X and nowhere earlier.

Aesthetic side by side: at equal size beside proposals/kf-2.png and assets/references/cercle1.webp, the page reads as a crisp black-and-white ink comic: solid black silhouettes, near-white neutral paper and screens, grey confined to backlit falloff, rear arches and the pane shadow; hand capitals in round tailed balloons; medium two-shots on a black floor band. It meets or beats kf-2 in craft (finer real profiles, lace, scissor edges) and is closer than kf-2 to the reference's black/white; page and film show identical art and lettering.

Legibility: balloon cap height >= 2% of page height (>= 27 px at 1350 px print page; >= 9 px when the page is shown 844 px wide on a landscape phone); every balloon readable in the film at 390 px display width.
Tone: pixels with luma 60-200 make up <= 30% of each page (kf-2: 42%; reference: 13%).

Dynamics and sound: bell swing energy < 2% of peak at the end of every panel cycle (each cycle ends on its page still); the film is <= 75 s and <= 6 MB; each panel's sound cue is the same PCM at both occurrences; page turns are audible and the p2-to-p3 turn is preceded by a dip to near-silence.
Hinge comparison: hinge-comparison.png/.md compares X opening p3 after the turn against X as the fifth panel of p2 (no turn) and states which placement makes the hand land as a surprise and why.

reader_questions: Read the four pages once at your normal pace. Which single panel changes how you understand the story? Name it by its page and position.
Is any drawing repeated? If so, which one means something different the second time, and what does it mean each time?
In the very last panel, what is the porter doing, and why?
Is there anything in the story that you see only once?
Does the second half feel like a new reading of the same events, or like a repeat? Say where you felt it.
intended_reading: The turning panel is X, the tall panel opening page 3 after the page turn: the caption 'THE BELL CAN ONLY BE RUNG FROM BEHIND THAT DOOR.' over the shadow of a hand behind the frosted glass of the service door pulling the bell cord. Someone hidden behind the never-opened service door rang the bell, not the visitor. The repeated drawing that changes most is A (the porter's outstretched arm, 'YOU! STAY RIGHT THERE.'): first an accusation that the newly arrived visitor rang the bell or is trespassing; last, protection, the porter holding the visitor back from the door whose occupant is calling. H ('THEN WHO RANG THE BELL?') also changes from a retort to a question with a dreadful answer, and G ('NOBODY GOES THROUGH THAT DOOR.') from a rule to a warning. The hand is seen only once; the door stays closed; the key is left on the bench.
